Pastel de Nata (known as egg tarts in the states) is a popular Portuguese pastry that can be found in just about every corner in Lisbon so of course I had to do some research in search of the best! Honestly they’re all delicious (well, most of them), and I think it comes down to preference of how you like your custard and how crunchy and caramelized you like it. They’re so accessible and easy to eat so I highly recommend doing the same when you’re in Portugal :)

_____

RED WINE CAKE RECIPE:

Ingredients
250g butter
250g sugar (this is the original recipe, we always use a bit less sugar)
4 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla sugar or vanilla extract (I show you how to make vanilla sugar here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-3fttVIy7qo&t=660s at the 2 minute mark)
2 teaspoons cocoa powder
1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon
250g flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
 125 millilitres red wine
pinch of salt

Method
Beat the butter until soft, then add the sugar, vanilla sugar and pinch of salt. Add the eggs bit by bit. Mix the flour with the baking powder and slowly add into the mixture. Then add the cocoa powder, cinnamon and red wine. 
Preheat the over to 180 degrees Celsius and grease your mold. Put the batter into the mold and bake the cake for 1 hour. 
After baking let the cake cool down and then put some icing sugar on top. Enjoy with a dollop of whipping cream.

RED WINE CAKE RECIPE:

Ingredients
250g butter
250g sugar (this is the original recipe, we always use a bit less sugar)
4 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla sugar or vanilla extract (I show you how to make vanilla sugar here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-3fttVIy7qo&t=660s at the 2 minute mark)
2 teaspoons cocoa powder
1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon
250g flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
 125 millilitres red wine
pinch of salt

Method
Beat the butter until soft, then add the sugar, vanilla sugar and pinch of salt. Add the eggs bit by bit. Mix the flour with the baking powder and slowly add into the mixture. Then add the cocoa powder, cinnamon and red wine. 
Preheat the over to 180 degrees Celsius and grease your mold. Put the batter into the mold and bake the cake for 1 hour. 
After baking let the cake cool down and then put some icing sugar on top. Enjoy with a dollop of whipping cream.
